_comment: Shared TypeScript config for the browser / Svelte profile: every federated
member under apps/, the federation host in shell/, and the three packages
that ship browser code — packages/federation, packages/gallery and
packages/workspace.
The scope line above used to stop at "apps/ plus shell/", which was true
when written and stale the moment anything else extended this file. It is
restated here because the packages were folded on 2026-09-13 and a config
that misdescribes its own consumers is how the next person picks the wrong
base.
SIBLING, NOT PARENT: tsconfig.services.json is the Node profile for
services/ — ES2022 without DOM, types node, unused-checks on. Neither file
extends the other; they are two profiles, and code belongs to exactly one.
Before this file the 17 apps carried three byte-distinct tsconfig.json
variants in an 8/7/2 split — drift, not intent. The two differences were
an extra 'src/**/*.d.ts' include (kept, it picks up css.d.ts) and a
missing useDefineForClassFields (kept as true, which is already the
default at target ES2022, so nothing changes for the two apps that
omitted it).
NOT to be confused with the root tsconfig.json, which is the fallback for
files no other project claims. It used to set jsx: react-jsx and target
ES2020; both were fixed once this base existed to compare it against.
Only compilerOptions live here. include/exclude deliberately stay in
each app: TypeScript resolves those paths relative to the file they are
WRITTEN in, not the one doing the extending, so a shared 'src/**/*.ts'
would resolve to '<root>/src/**/*.ts' and every app would compile zero
files. Verified the hard way.
